chunk_findings.detail: `Checked.notify` is documented as `{id, holder, state}` ("Who is told, for a link onto a record somebody is working"), and `_point` is the only place that ever populates it — but it sets only `{"id": chosen.target, "state": record_state(...)[1]}`. The `holder` key is never produced. Concretely: claim task `T` as `alice`, then add a similar task and answer `extends T`. `extendable` returns False (active lease), so `_point`'s `else` branch runs and `notify` becomes `{"id": "T", "state": "claimed by alice"}`. Any consumer that follows the documented shape (`chk.notify["holder"]`, exposed via `Checked.data()` as `out["holder"] = self.notify`) has no holder id to notify and hits `KeyError` — the only place the holder survives is inside the free‑text `state` string `"claimed by alice"`, which is explicitly documented as a human‑readable rendering, not a machine value. The intent ("X claimed/in progress/closed -> new record linked to X and the holder told") therefore cannot be satisfied from the payload the check returns. To match the contract, `_point` needs to record the holder (e.g. `it.lease.holder` for a claimed task/phase) alongside `id` and `state`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/_dedupe.py:_point (the `out.notify = {...}` assignment)

chunk_findings.detail:
The "new record linked to X and the holder told" outcome for a duplicate/extends of a claimed/in-progress/closed record is unreachable for an exact re‑file, because the caller computes the new record's id as `bid = id or auto_id("B", summary, item)` and appends under that id. `auto_id` is a pure function of `summary`+`item`, so when the re‑filed text equals X's text the id is equal to X's id — the code's own comment confirms this ("the same summary and item give the same auto id"). The appended `bug.found` event therefore merges into the existing closed/claimed X (see `_h_bug_found`) instead of creating a distinct record, and the function then returns `prior.resolution`:

    log.append("bug.found", bid, {"item": item, "summary": summary, **chk.fields})
    ...
    prior = st.bugs.get(bid)
    if prior is not None and prior.resolution:
        return O.ok("bug.found", id=bid, resolution=prior.resolution, **chk.data())

Concretely: file bug B (summary S, item I), fix it, then call `bug_found(repo, summary=S, item=I)` (auto‑duplicate, score 1.0). Expected per the stated acceptance ("on a fixed bug it files a new linked bug", "exact re-filing auto-links") is a NEW bug record linked to B; actual is that the event merges into B and the old resolution is returned — the recurrence vanishes, exactly the failure the feature was meant to remove. The claimed/in‑progress variant has the same problem (the recurrence is absorbed into the claimed record rather than filed as a linked bug). The caller never consults any fresh id that `DD.check_add`/`chk` may have produced, and it also never reaches `DD.extend`, since a closed target is categorized as "new record linked", not an extension. A `chk`-supplied id (or a distinct id for the non-extension duplicate case) would be needed for this branch to produce the promised record.

chunk_findings.detail: On the extension / auto-duplicate path the function returns before the `tags` handling is ever reached, so a caller-supplied `tags` is silently discarded, whereas the new-record path applies it (`data["tags"] = csv_list(tags)`). This is reachable without any explicit answer: when `DD.check_add` scores an existing memory at 1.0 it is "recorded as duplicate without asking", i.e. `chk.extension` is set, and `memory_add` short-circuits into `DD.extend(log, cfg, chk, "memory.recorded")` — which receives no `tags` and no `data`, so the requested tags can never be merged into the existing memory. Concrete input: first `memory add "build uses bazel"` (memory now exists with no tags), then `memory add "build uses bazel" --tags build`. The check scores 1.0, `chk.extension` is truthy, the function returns at the extension branch, and the memory is left untagged instead of gaining the `build` tag the user asked for. This also contradicts the retained comment on the `tags` block (which exists specifically because a fact's tags must be correctable), and is inconsistent with the `related`/`new` paths, where the identical `--tags build` invocation does apply the tag.

chunk_findings.detail:
The line

    assert A.bug_found(repo, summary=title, item="T1", id="Bx", agent="a").exit == 3 or True

is a tautology. Python parses `==` before `or`, so this is `(exit == 3) or True`, which is always truthy regardless of what `bug_found` returns. The assertion therefore verifies nothing: the test's own name ("asks nothing") implies the expected exit is `0`, yet even if the implementation returned any exit code, wrote `Bx`, or raised no refusal at all, this line would still pass. Concretely, if the dedupe path in `bug_found` is broken for the `--item` case (e.g. it refuses with exit 3 when it should not, or silently writes `Bx` when it should not), this test will not catch it. The intent of the scenario — that filing a bug whose text matches the task that fixes it must not be treated as a duplicate — is not actually exercised by this line. It should assert the concrete expected outcome (and, if the "no write" part matters, verify `"Bx" not in state(repo).bugs`).
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_add_dedupe.py:189 (`test_a_bug_filed_against_the_task_that_fixes_it_asks_nothing`)

chunk_findings.detail: `Checked` documents `notify` as `{id, holder, state}` and the change's stated goal is that when an answer points at a record that is claimed/in-progress/closed, "the holder [is] told". But `_point` only ever builds `out.notify = {"id": chosen.target, "state": record_state(...)[1]}` — the `holder` key is never set. Given input: answer `extends T` where `T` is a task in state `open` with an active lease held by `alice`; `record_state` returns state `"claimed by alice"` and `_point` stores `{"id": T, "state": "claimed by alice"}`. Downstream code that follows the documented contract and reads `chk.notify["holder"]` (or `Checked.data()["holder"]["holder"]`) raises `KeyError`, and there is no usable agent id to notify; the holder identity survives only as a substring of a display string.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/_dedupe.py `_point` / `Checked.notify`

chunk_findings.detail: `record_state` renders a decision's status as `dc.status or "active"`, i.e. a decision with no status (or status `"active"`) is shown to the user as an active decision. But `extendable` only accepts decisions whose status is literally in `("accepted", "proposed")`, so such a decision is treated as non-extendable. Given an active, non-superseded decision `D` created with the default/empty status, answering `extends D` on a new decision falls into the `else` branch of `_point`: it does **not** append the text to `D` and instead files a brand-new decision linked to it, contradicting `extendable`'s own docstring ("a lesson or decision not superseded") and the intent that an answer onto an open record adds to it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/_dedupe.py `extendable` (decision branch) / `record_state` (decision branch)

chunk_findings.detail: The duplicate decision is computed from the pre-transaction snapshot `st` (`chk = DD.check_add(repo, log, cfg, st, ...)`), and that decision — including `chk.fields` written into the record and the "extends X" branch — is then applied without re-validating it inside the transaction. The transaction only re-checks the primary key via `_taken(_fresh(log), item, ...)`, which protects same-id collisions but not the text-based dedupe. Concrete interleaving: two concurrent `task_add` calls with distinct ids `T1`/`T2` and identical text both execute `DD.check_add` before either commits; both see no candidate and both reach `log.append`, producing two records the dedupe was supposed to refuse (the second call run sequentially would have been refused). Likewise `bug`/`task` "extends X" decisions are acted on (`DD.extend(...)`) entirely outside any transaction, so a concurrent close/claim of X yields an extension of a closed/claimed record instead of the "new linked record" the intent specifies. To be correct the check (or at least a re-validation of `chk`) must run after `_fresh(log)` inside the transaction.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/items.py:phase_add / task_add (DD.check_add evaluated outside `log.transaction()`)

chunk_findings.detail:
The first assertion in this test is `assert A.bug_found(repo, summary=title, item="T1", id="Bx", agent="a").exit == 3 or True`. Since `==` binds tighter than `or`, the expression is `(exit == 3) or True`, which is unconditionally true. The assertion can never fail, so the contract the test's own name asserts ("asks nothing" — i.e. a bug filed against the task that fixes it must not be refused) is not verified at all: it passes whether `bug_found` returns `exit == 3`, `exit == 0`, or anything else.

Worse, the call is not side-effect free and is not isolated from the rest of the test. Under the intended behaviour the call succeeds and writes bug `Bx` with `summary == title` into `repo` (the fixture `repo` is function scoped, so it persists for the remainder of this test). The next lines then file `By` with `summary=title + " today"` and assert `out.exit == 0` because the top candidate is `T1`:

    out = A.bug_found(repo, summary=title + " today", item="T1", id="By", agent="a")
    assert out.exit == 0, out.reason
    assert out.data["candidates"][0]["id"] == "T1"

At that point `Bx` is itself a bug in the log with a summary nearly identical to `By`'s and with the same `item=T1`, so the matcher has a much closer candidate than the task `T1`; under the autouse `DDFLOW_DEDUPE_ON_MATCH=ask` this can legitimately refuse (`exit == 3`) or report `Bx` as `candidates[0]`, and the test fails. Conversely if `bug_found` *does* wrongly refuse the first call, the vacuous assertion hides it and the second assertion is trivially satisfied after `Bx` was never written. Either way the `or True` masks a real regression while introducing an order/state dependence between the two calls.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_add_dedupe.py::test_a_bug_filed_against_the_task_that_fixes_it_asks_nothing (the `assert ... .exit == 3 or True` line)

chunk_findings.detail:
`O.Refusal` is an exception type: the very same `decision_add` raises it a few lines earlier for the missing-decision validation (`raise O.Refusal(...)`), and the CLI is built to translate a raised `O.Refusal` into exit status 3. The new duplicate path instead **returns** the refusal object (`if chk.refusal is not None: return chk.refusal`), which never triggers that exception handling.

Concrete failure: give `decision_add` the acceptance input — a draft whose text re-files record `B5d98a4da0a` with no `answer`. `DD.check_add` sets `chk.refusal` (top candidate `B3eda99e0fe`), and `decision_add` returns that refusal object as its result instead of raising it. The caller, which only maps raised `O.Refusal` to exit 3, either reports success (exit 0) or blows up trying to treat the exception object as an `O.Outcome` when it reads `.kind`/`.code`; in neither case does the required "refused (exit 3)" behavior occur, so the acceptance test still fails. The branch should be `raise chk.refusal` (contrast the extension branch, which correctly returns only on success).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/decisions.py:decision_add (`return chk.refusal`)

chunk_findings.detail:
Both add paths load state once with `_load()` and then run `DD.check_add(...)` *before* entering `with log.transaction():`, using that pre-transaction `st`. The id-collision test is deliberately re-verified against the live log inside the transaction (`taken = _taken(_fresh(log), item, readd=readd)`), but the duplicate check is not. The result of the pre-transaction check (`chk.fields`, and `DD.after_add`) is what actually gets written, so any record that appears between `_load()` and the commit is invisible to dedupe.

Concrete interleaving: agent A calls `task_add(repo, item="A1", title=T, body=B)` and agent B calls `task_add(repo, item="B1", title=T, body=B)` at the same moment. Both execute `_load()` before either transaction commits, so both `check_add` calls see no matching record and return the "new" answer (extension==False). The transactions serialize the writes but nothing re-runs the match, so both records are written with no `duplicate_of`/`related` link and no answer recorded. Since a score-1.0 match against an open+unclaimed record is supposed to auto-extend that record (no new id) or link to it, B should have extended/linked to A; instead the exact duplicates this change exists to prevent are produced. The same holds for `phase_add`. The match (or at least a re-match of `chk` against `_fresh(log)`) needs to happen inside the transaction alongside the `_taken` re-check.

chunk_findings.detail: The test is named and documented (and the intent states) that an `extends` answer on a fixed/closed bug files a new linked bug, but it passes `answer=DD.Answer("duplicate_of", "B5d98a4da0a")` rather than `Answer("extends", ...)`. Because `duplicate_of` is a distinct answer, the test never exercises the extends-on-closed path. A regression where `extends` on a fixed bug incorrectly appends to the closed record, omits the holder notification, or uses the wrong link relation would still pass this test. The demonstration input is the answer value itself: replace it with `DD.Answer("extends", "B5d98a4da0a")` and the test would then check the claimed scenario.
chunk_findings.title: `tests/test_add_dedupe.py::test_extends_a_fixed_bug_files_a_new_linked_bug`

chunk_findings.detail: The test name promises coverage for session prompts, and the intent says session prompts/notes are never checked, but the test only calls `A.session_note` twice. It never invokes the session-prompt add path. If the implementation incorrectly ran the dedupe check for session prompts, this test would still pass. A concrete missing input is adding the same prompt text twice through the prompt API; the test never supplies it.
chunk_findings.title: `tests/test_add_dedupe.py::test_session_notes_and_prompts_are_never_checked`

chunk_findings.detail: The fixture’s docstring says the log holds the fixture records “except B3eda99e0fe”, but the filter is `if rec["added"] >= FIX["B3eda99e0fe"]["added"]: continue`. That excludes not only B3eda99e0fe but any record with the same `added` timestamp or any later record. If the corpus contains a tie on that timestamp, the reconstructed log is incomplete, the engine’s rarity-weighted similarity scores change, and `test_refiling_a_real_report_is_refused_with_the_original_as_candidate` can fail or choose a different top candidate. A concrete input is two corpus records with the same `added` value as B3eda99e0fe: both are dropped, though the stated intent is to drop only B3eda99e0fe.
chunk_findings.title: `tests/test_add_dedupe.py::corpus_repo`
